scenario.name: Splunk STRT & Huntress — ConnectWise ScreenConnect "SlashAndGrab" Auth Bypass & RMM RCE
scenario.shortSubtitle: Splunk STRT / Huntress · CVE-2024-1709 /SetupWizard.aspx/ Traversal, User.xml Overwrite & .ashx RCE
scenario.overview: Imagine a high-ceiling logistics warehouse with towering steel pallet racks stacked with labeled shipping crates, clipboard dock stations, and a bright yellow forklift cruising down the aisle. Inside the bustling logistics warehouse, an unverified driver climbs into a parked yellow forklift and rolls toward the high-bay customer storage racks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the loading dock check-out clipboards blending in with everyday guests, then smuggles copied records out past the loading dock check-out clipboards in tiny disguised batches. The warehouse barcode inventory system flashes an urgent alert when hundreds of customer pallets are relabeled in minutes outside normal shift hours. In this scenario (CVE-2024-1709, Splunk STRT & Huntress, ConnectWise ScreenConnect "SlashAndGrab" Auth Bypass & RMM RCE), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: accessing "/SetupWizard.aspx/anything", then submitting the Setup Form to Overwrite, then abusing the RMM Console to Push SYSTEM. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Accessing "/SetupWizard.aspx/anything", then Submitting the Setup Form to Overwrite, then Abusing the RMM Console to Push SYSTEM, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: SETUPWIZARD.ASPX/ TRAVERSAL & USER.XML OVERWRITE (CVE-2024-1709)
stages.subtitle: Accessing /SetupWizard.aspx/ to overwrite App_Data\User.xml
stages.description: Inside the bustling logistics warehouse, an unverified driver climbs into a parked yellow forklift and rolls toward the high-bay customer storage racks. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the loading dock check-out clipboards blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the warehouse dispatcher go about their routine. As reverse-engineered by Huntress, to block access to the initial setup page after Day 1, ScreenConnect’s authentication filter checked whether the requested URL ended with the exact string /SetupWizard.aspx. By simply adding a trailing slash or suffix, GET /SetupWizard.aspx/anything, the string-ending check returns false and lets the request through without authentication, while Microsoft’s ASP.NET web engine still routes the request to SetupWizard.aspx (treating the trailing "/anything" as harmless Request.PathInfo metadata, CVE-2024-1709). In ASP.NET, a URL like /Page.aspx/extra is routed to the handler for /Page.aspx with Request.PathInfo set to "/extra". Because the security check tested Request.Path instead of Request.FilePath, a single trailing "/" bypassed the lock completely. In the documented Sysmon EID 11 exchange from Threat Actor (BlackBasta / LockBit) to DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap, DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap responds with ACK CVE-2024-1709 (confirming that the OVERWRITE USER.XML request succeeded on DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 MALICIOUS .ASHX EXTENSION UPLOAD & SYSTEM RCE). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ OVERWRITE USER.XML / ⇠#1 ACK CVE-2024-1709) from Node ① (#1 Threat Actor (BlackBasta / LockBit)) to Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

stages.title: MALICIOUS .ASHX EXTENSION UPLOAD & SYSTEM RCE
stages.subtitle: Installing rogue extension in App_Extensions\ to spawn cmd.exe as SYSTEM
stages.description: Lifting stacked pallets off the shelves, the driver slaps a brand-new shipping barcode and their own heavy padlock onto every customer crate in the bay. Here in Step 2 inside the logistics warehouse, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the high-bay pallet racks & forklift without disturbing the quarantined audit cage. With the first-time setup wizard open in their browser, the attacker submits a new administrator username and password. ScreenConnect immediately overwrites C:\Program Files (x86)\ScreenConnect\App_Data\User.xml (the local XML database file that stores all administrator accounts and password hashes on the server, wiping out the company’s legitimate IT administrators and logging the attacker straight in as the sole Super-Admin). Furthermore, attackers can chain CVE-2024-1708 (a ZipSlip path-traversal flaw in ScreenConnect’s Extension uploader that writes .ashx webshells directly into App_Extensions\ for server-side persistence). Because the Setup Wizard was designed for a fresh installation, completing the wizard resets App_Data\User.xml from scratch (overwriting existing administrator hashes with attacker-chosen credentials) and returns an authenticated administrator session cookie to the caller (granting full web console control without knowing prior passwords). Mechanically, defenders treat this stage as complete only after the T1505.003 control point is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving prior-stage output now drives the next action) and confirmed in host or network telemetry (the channel that timestamps the handoff). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ASHX EXTENSION RCE / ⇠#2 ACK PID 5912) from Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap) to Node ③ (#3 ConnectWise ScreenConnect Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

stages.title: DOWNSTREAM FLEET COMMAND PUSH OVER TCP 8041
stages.subtitle: Pushing .cmd scripts to managed endpoints via ScreenConnect ClientService
stages.description: When the real warehouse dispatcher arrives for morning pickup, every pallet is locked behind someone else’s key and rerouted toward an unknown loading dock. In this final step inside the logistics warehouse, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the loading dock check-out clipboards in tiny disguised batches until the warehouse barcode inventory log catches the mismatch. Why is compromising an RMM server so catastrophic? Because every laptop and server managed by the IT team has the ScreenConnect client agent (ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe, a trusted background service running with full NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges) permanently connected to this server. From their hijacked admin console, the attacker selects all connected computers and broadcasts PowerShell or ransomware commands (which each endpoint agent writes into C:\Windows\Temp\ScreenConnect\<version>\*.cmd and executes immediately as SYSTEM). Without needing a single exploit on the client workstations, the operator uses the built-in Backstage command runner (a legitimate remote-management console hidden from the logged-in desktop user) to execute arbitrary commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM across hundreds or thousands of managed endpoints simultaneously (turning one RMM server compromise into fleet-wide code execution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ FLEET MASS PUSH / ⇠#3 ACK Fleet Push) from Node ③ (#3 ConnectWise ScreenConnect Server) to Node ④ (#4 Malicious .ashx Extension & csc.exe), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

detectionRule.title: Splunk STRT — ConnectWise ScreenConnect User.xml or .ashx Creation (CVE-2024-1709)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 User.xml or Extension Creation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ScreenConnect.Service.exe'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\ScreenConnect\App_Data\User.xml'
      - '\ScreenConnect\App_Extensions\'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Upgrade ConnectWise ScreenConnect to version 23.9.8 or later immediately and audit App_Data\User.xml and App_Extensions\ for unauthorized modifications.

detectionRule.title: ScreenConnect Server Service Spawning Command Shell (CVE-2024-1709 RCE)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect Server Spawning Shell Process
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\ScreenConnect.Service.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Isolate the ScreenConnect server if ScreenConnect.Service.exe spawns a command shell and inspect App_Extensions\ for rogue .ashx files.

detectionRule.title: ScreenConnect Client Executing Script from Windows Temp Directory
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: ScreenConnect ClientService Script Execution in Temp
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
